issues.description: The UML in the problem statement shows the Animal(String) constructor with a '-' (private) visibility, but the intended design requires a non-private constructor so subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat) can call it. The solution implements a public Animal(String) constructor, and the template Main expects to instantiate subclasses (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")) which would be impossible if the superclass constructor were private. This discrepancy in constructor visibility in the UML can confuse students and would prevent correct subclassing if followed literally.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML in problem_statement.md to show the Animal(String) constructor as public (use '+' instead of '-') and/or clarify in the text that subclasses must be able to call the constructor. This ensures students understand the constructor must be accessible to derived classes.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement shows addAnimal(Animal) with a '-' (private) visibility, while the textual description and solution expect addAnimal to be callable to add animals to the farm (the Main template calls farm.addAnimal(...)). The solution implements addAnimal as public. Marking addAnimal private in the UML would contradict the described API and prevent typical usage from outside the Farm class.
issues.suggestedFix: Correct the UML in problem_statement.md to mark addAnimal(Animal) as public (use '+') and/or state in the text that addAnimal should be a public API. This aligns the diagram with the intended usage shown in Main and the solution implementation.
